fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: Windows creator bg3.exe+0x188F8C0 (AllocRaw 0x10) stores a 32-bit 0 here. Live 2 and 6 - a small state enum (the system bg3.exe+0x195F4A0 queries it together with eoc::death::StateComponent, whose Script Extender layout is one uint32_t State). Readers (macOS): ecl::timeline::ArenaDecisionSystem, gui::CapabilitiesSystem::Update; the Toolkit ActiveEventSystemHelper::HasDeathSavingThrowEnded only tests its presence.

fields.name: DeathType
fields.evidence: macOS ecl::death::CharacterSystem::Update compares eoc::death::DeathTypeComponent with the byte at StateComponent+4 and issues ecl::death::SetVisualImmediateRequestOneFrameComponent when they differ (a cached copy of the death type); Windows creator bg3.exe+0x188F8C0 writes one byte at +4, live 0x0B / 0x03 (DeathType values). Offset +4 from macOS is a hint, the Windows byte store agrees. | first pass: Windows creator bg3.exe+0x188F8C0 stores one byte 0 at +4. Live 0x0B / 0x03.

fields.name: _Pad5
fields.evidence: Not written by the Windows creator (live 00 CE 01 / FF FF FF): padding after the byte at +4.

fields.name: field_8
fields.evidence: Windows creator writes one 8-byte store of 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF at +8 (macOS: the same with a vector register). Live -1.

fields.name: field_c
fields.evidence: Second half of the 8-byte -1 store at +8. Live -1.

open_questions: Whether +8 is one 64-bit value or two int32 (the Windows creator writes it with a single 8-byte store of -1); no Windows reader of the members was found (bg3.exe+0x195F4A0 only registers the query of the client death system).
Meanings of the state value and of the byte at +4.
names pass 2: field_0 (state enum, live 2/6), field_8 / field_c (-1) not named.
second_pass: The Windows creator bg3.exe+0x188F8C0 fixes a 32-bit +0, a byte at +4 (so +5..+7 is padding) and an 8-byte -1 at +8; the split of +8 and all meanings stay open.
